articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals in Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations, and Cuba
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 5, 2026, targeting entities and individuals involved in cyber-related activities, transnational criminal organizations, and those connected to Cuba.

This action includes the publication of a Cuba-related determination, further solidifying U.S. sanctions policy against the Cuban regime. The specific details of the designated parties and the nature of their illicit activities were not immediately released but are expected to be detailed on the OFAC website.

These designations underscore the U.S. government's ongoing efforts to combat malicious cyber activities, disrupt international criminal networks, and pressure the Cuban government through economic measures.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations, Amends Venezuela General License, and Issues Iran Alert
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates to existing listings on November 4, 2026. This action is accompanied by the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert titled 'Iranian Shadow Fleet Reliance on False Flags for Sanctions Evasion,' highlighting tactics used to circumvent sanctions.

Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License 5AA, 'Authorizing Certain Transactions Related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 Percent Bond on or After December 18, 2026,' and an amended Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 595).

General License 5AA further delays the effectiveness of the authorization in GL 5 until December 18, 2026, meaning transactions related to the sale or transfer of CITGO shares in connection with the PdVSA 2020 8.5 percent bond remain prohibited until that date, unless specifically authorized by OFAC.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License FF-1 for International Development Bank for Investment and Finance
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued Iran General License FF-1 on October 29, 2026, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, also known as Iraq Development Bank.
This amended general license replaces and supersedes General License FF and sets a wind-down period through December 1, 2026.
The new license also specifies that payments to blocked persons must be made into blocked accounts, reinforcing compliance requirements during the wind-down phase.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities Supporting North Korean IT Worker Schemes and DRC Instability
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting individuals and entities connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Under its North Korea sanctions program, OFAC sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for supporting North Korean government-run IT worker schemes. These schemes reportedly defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for North Korea's weapons programs through the use of fraudulent identities and deceptive tactics to secure employment.

Separately, OFAC also imposed designations related to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, sanctioning the Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a Rwandan financial institution, for facilitating Rwanda's support for the March 23 Movement (M23) and its political wing in eastern DRC.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme exported networking equipment and related services from the United States to Joint Stock Company (JSC) Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer. MMZA was majority-owned by the designated Russian state-owned company JSC Concern Almaz-Antey, rendering MMZA a blocked person by operation of law, even though MMZA itself was not on the SDN List until June 2022.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were egregious but voluntarily self-disclosed. The settlement emphasizes the importance of sanctions-related diligence during acquisitions, vigilance regarding sanctions risks, and adequate oversight of foreign operations.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends 11 Frequently Asked Questions on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) amended 11 of its Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026, as part of an ongoing review to ensure published guidance remains current.

The revised FAQs address critical areas including which jurisdictions are subject to broad sanctions, how to block an account or funds transfer, the interest required on blocked funds, and when to reject rather than block a transaction.

The updates also clarify notification procedures for customers when property is blocked, rules for account openings and transactions involving blocked persons, and the timing and procedures for reporting blocked property and rejected transactions, including the required format for Annual Reports of Blocked Property.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations, and Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC removed certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea from its Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List.

Specifically, OFAC delisted Chinese national Lu Hezheng and two Chinese entities, Shanghai Moxing Cultural Media Co. Ltd. and Shanghai Hongman Cartoon and Animation Design Studio, previously sanctioned for ties to a North Korean government-run animation studio. Belarusian national Andrei Alekseevich Rybakov was also delisted from the Belarus sanctions program.

Additionally, OFAC issued new Iran-related General Licenses GG and HH, and Russia-related General Licenses 128D and 130B, along with amended Frequently Asked Questions, signaling adjustments to various sanctions programs.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026.

These designations are accompanied by the issuance of associated General Licenses, which aim to provide guidance and authorization for certain transactions that might otherwise be prohibited under the new sanctions.
This action underscores the U.S. government's commitment to combating intellectual property theft and leveraging sanctions to protect American innovation and economic security.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief Efforts
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued Venezuela-related General License 60A on October 16, 2026, titled 'Authorizing Transactions Related to Earthquake Relief Efforts in Venezuela.'

This general license authorizes all transactions related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations, including the payment of taxes, tolls, and fees to the Government of Venezuela connected with such relief efforts.
Additionally, OFAC issued one amended Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1263, to provide further clarity on the scope and application of this authorization.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates 16 Individuals and 10 Entities in Iran, Sanctions Cuban State-Owned Bank
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 15, 2026, adding 16 individuals and 10 entities to its sanctions list.

These designations include the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance (also known as Iraq Development Bank) in Baghdad, Chabahar International Bank Overseas Company, and Jazireh International Bank Company in Iran, along with several exchange companies such as Abolhasan Jalali and Partners Exchange Company and Bavi and Partners Exchange Company.

Concurrently, OFAC designated the Cuban state-owned Banco Internacional de Comercio, S.A. (BICSA) and issued new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions related to Iran, Cuba, and Russia.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Fined $1,529,685 by OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) to settle its potential civil liability for nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

The violations involved the export of networking equipment and related services from the United States to a Russian defense manufacturer that was majority-owned by a designated Russian state-owned company, making it a blocked person by operation of law.
OFAC determined that the apparent violations were egregious but voluntarily self-disclosed, leading to the settlement amount.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.
